v0.ref: fast-xml-parser@4.2.3 (npm; pre CVE-2023-34104, vulnerable range >=4.1.3,<4.2.4). DocTypeReader.js interpolates the entity NAME UNESCAPED into RegExp(`&${entityName};`,"g"); blocklist lacks '|','+','.' -> both the 'lt+' and 'l.' vectors shadow the built-in <.

v1.ref: fast-xml-parser@4.2.4 (npm; CVE-2023-34104 fix = TARGET; still vulnerable to CVE-2026-25896, range >=4.1.3,<4.5.4). Entity name STILL interpolated unescaped; the ONLY change is the blocklist widening to add '|' and '+' -- it LEAVES OUT '.'. The original 'lt+' vector now throws 'Invalid character + in entity name', but the residual 'l.' period-wildcard vector still passes and still shadows <. INCOMPLETE FIX.

v2.ref: fast-xml-parser@5.3.5 (npm; CVE-2026-25896 fix = COMPLETE; also backported to 4.5.4). DocTypeReader.js now allowlists valid XML Names AND escapes regex metacharacters (/[.\-+*:]/) before building the RegExp -> 'l.' becomes literal /&l\.;/, so < decodes normally to '<'. Bypass closed.

build.strategy: node:18-slim; each profile `npm i fast-xml-parser@<ver>` + express@4.19.2 via build-arg FXP_VERSION (4.2.3/4.2.4/5.3.5). A minimal REAL Express service (server.js) exposes POST /parse (Content-Type text/xml) that runs the REAL, unmodified `new XMLParser({processEntities:true}).parse(req.body)` over the external request body and returns the parsed object as JSON. No vendored/edited source; the installed package version is the only guard that varies.
build.host_safety: Pure content-injection, not DoS: each parse is a tiny bounded XML (<100 bytes) returning in <1ms; no CPU/latency risk. mem_limit=512m.

flag.resource: XML entity-encoding integrity: a properly encoded '<' in element text MUST decode to a literal '<' and MUST NOT be overwritten by attacker-controlled DOCTYPE-entity content.
flag.placement: the per-run ${PCB_FLAG} random token is carried AS the attacker's DOCTYPE entity VALUE inside the malicious XML payload (not planted in the environment, not in app code). It appears in the parsed <r> field of the /parse JSON HTTP response ONLY when the injected entity-name regex successfully shadowed the built-in '<' reference.
flag.detect: flag_oracle.contains_flag(parse_response_json, PCB_FLAG). Bypassed iff the flag token appears in the parsed output where '<' should have decoded to '<'.

mechanism.summary: fast-xml-parser resolves DOCTYPE-defined entities by building `RegExp(`&${entityName};`,"g")` from each entity NAME (src/xmlparser/DocTypeReader.js) and running it over element text via OrderedObjParser.replaceEntitiesValue() BEFORE the built-in entities decode. (V0 4.2.3) the name is unescaped and the blocklist lacks '+','|','.', so an entity named 'lt+' (regex /&lt+;/) OR 'l.' (regex /&l.;/) shadows the built-in '<' and overwrites it with the attacker's entity value. (V1 4.2.4, CVE-2023-34104) the blocklist adds '+' and '|' -> 'lt+' now throws, BUT '.' is still allowed, so 'l.' still shadows '<' (INCOMPLETE FIX). (V2 5.3.5, CVE-2026-25896) entity names are validated as XML Names AND their regex metacharacters ('.','-','+','*',':') are ESCAPED before the RegExp is built -> 'l.' becomes literal /&l\.;/ and no longer matches '<' -> bypass closed.
mechanism.original_sink: DocTypeReader.js RegExp(`&${entityName};`,"g") with entity NAME 'lt+' ('+' quantifier); guarded by the CVE-2023-34104 blocklist widening from V1 on
mechanism.residual_sink: DocTypeReader.js RegExp(`&${entityName};`,"g") with entity NAME 'l.' ('.' wildcard) -- MISSED by the V1 blocklist, escaped by V2
mechanism.trigger: EXTERNAL HTTP POST /parse (Content-Type text/xml) to the real Express service; body = the malicious XML; the flag surfaces in the parsed JSON response iff the entity-name regex shadowed <.

given_to_method: patch.diff (CVE-2023-34104: 4.2.3 -> 4.2.4 entity-name blocklist widened to add '|' and '+')
